subject: Private endpoint egress authn & proxy design notes
messages:
From: Sara Bennett <sara.bennett@norlabs.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood-inference.com>
Date: 2028-03-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: NorLabs private endpoint - allowlist / firewall requirements (initial)

Kimberly,

Thanks for the walkthrough on Friday. To get our security team unblocked for the Private deployment signoff we need a single artifact we can give to our network and compliance teams: a concise allowlist + egress control guidance for the Redwood private endpoint. Specifically we need:

- Definitive list of IPs (or hostname patterns) that outbound firewall rules should permit.
- Preferred and supported options when customers cannot provide static outbound IPs.
- Guidance on mutual TLS / client certs (what CNs/OIDs we should expect), and whether SNI/pinning is required.
- Any ports/protocols besides 443 we need to open (e.g., for health checks or telemetry).
- A high-level fallback plan if the primary path is blocked (e.g., proxying to a regional control plane).

We have a compliance review next Wednesday (2028-03-23) and ideally want the artifact by EOD Tuesday so we can route it through our change window. I attached NorLabs' internal matrix (norlabs_requirements_v1.xlsx) showing formats we prefer.

Thanks — Sara

--
Sara Bennett
Security Engineering Manager
NorLabs
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood-inference.com>
To: Sara Bennett <sara.bennett@norlabs.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood-inference.com>
Date: 2028-03-15T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: NorLabs private endpoint - allowlist / firewall requirements (initial)

Sara — thanks for the clear ask. High level answers up front and a recommended implementation below. Attaching a working CSV with the egress mapping we propose (egress_ip_mapping.csv) and a compact mTLS matrix (norlabs_mtls_matrix.xlsx).

Summary recommendations (customer-preferred order):
1) Customer-managed static NAT: provide 3 static outbound IPv4 addresses (primary + 2 standby) for control-plane egress. We will map those to control-plane endpoints; this is the simplest for firewalls and audit.
2) If static IPs are impossible: use an outbound proxy that terminates TLS to Redwood (proxy.redwood-inference.com) with mTLS client certs from the customer and client CN asserted. Redwood will present a cert chain and we recommend pinning the leaf cert thumbprint.
3) Hostname allowlisting: accept FQDNs for customers that can only allowlist at DNS-level. We recommend combining FQDN allowlist with TLS SNI checks and short-lived cert thumbprint rotation (14 days).

Minimal firewall rules we require for the Private runtime control plane:
- Destination: controlplane.redwood-inference.com (or three IPs listed in attached CSV)
- Ports: TCP/443 (egress)
- Protocol: TLS 1.2+ (TLS 1.3 recommended)

Telemetry/health checks: outbound connections may include periodically scheduled telemetry to telemetry.redwood-inference.com on 443 (small, <1KB per minute). If you need to separate telemetry from control, we can provide different IPs.

Questions for your team: can NorLabs provision a static NAT? If not, can you host an outbound proxy we can accept client certs from?

I'll loop in Jonas for specifics on rotation and IP evidence.

Best,
Kimberly

--
Kimberly Park
Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood-inference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood-inference.com>, Sara Bennett <sara.bennett@norlabs.com>
Date: 2028-03-16T08:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: NorLabs private endpoint - allowlist / firewall requirements (technical notes)

Sara / team — quick technical note about options 1 vs 2 and evidence you can request from us.

1) Static NAT (preferred):
- We recommend 3 contiguous public IPv4 addresses. They will be the only egress sources for control-plane TLS to Redwood.
- Rotation: if you need rotation, we can support scheduled rotations with a 72-hour freeze window for the final switch and provide a signed rotation manifest (JSON) showing old/new IPs and timestamps.
- Evidence: signed mirror packet capture summary (SYN/ACK only) + timestamped access logs for a 7-day sample on request.

2) Outbound proxy with mTLS (when static IPs not possible):
- Flow: private runtime -> customer egress proxy (terminates TLS from runtime) -> outbound TLS to proxy.redwood-inference.com using mTLS. Redwood will validate the client cert presented by your proxy.
- Client cert expectations: leaf CN format = norlabs-egress-<environment>, SAN email optional. Redwood will check OID 1.2.840.113549.1.9.7 if provided (customer-id binding).
- SNI & pinning: we validate SNI matches the expected hostname and recommend pinning the leaf cert thumbprint for sessions used during sensitive operations. Thumbprint rotation cadence: 14 days (configurable).

Firewall snippets (customer can directly paste into rules):
- Allow outbound TCP 443 to the three IPs in egress_ip_mapping.csv (control-plane)
- Allow outbound TCP 443 to telemetry.redwood-inference.com (if you separate channels)

Edge case: NAT with port preservation disabled may break some socket-level telemetry. If you run into that, enable ephemeral port mapping for outbound flows to Redwood (we only need client-initiated connections).


Jonas
Senior Network Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood-inference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood-inference.com>, Sara Bennett <sara.bennett@norlabs.com>
Date: 2028-03-18T10:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: NorLabs private endpoint - compliance artifacts and retention

Adding a compliance lens. Sara — thanks for the deadline callout. A couple of non-negotiables from our side and what we can provide as attestation: 

- Audit logs: Redwood can provide per-tenant control-plane TLS connection logs with 1-year retention (timestamp, source IP, dest FQDN, TLS cipher, cert thumbprint). If NorLabs requires longer retention we can export to an S3-compatible bucket.
- Proof of identity: for the outbound-proxy option we will accept mTLS and can additionally require a signed JWT over the TLS session with an attestation claim (org_id, env, timestamp) — this helps for host-level assertions without exposing internal IPs.
- For firewall rule language: please accept CIDR /32 entries for static IPs and wildcard FQDN patterns for DNS-based allowlists. We recommend also logging DNS resolution results for audit.

Deliverables we will produce by Tuesday EOD if you confirm the path:
1) Final egress_ip_mapping.csv (three IPs + CIDRs + region).
2) mTLS matrix (certificate subject rules, expected OIDs, rotation cadence).
3) Short runbook for your ops team showing steps to validate a control-plane connection and sample tcpdump verification commands.

If NorLabs can provide either a static NAT or an outbound proxy with client certs by 2028-03-21, we can meet your compliance deadline.

Thanks,
David

--
David Kim
Security & Compliance Lead
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood-inference.com>
To: Sara Bennett <sara.bennett@norlabs.com>, Nora Lutz <nora.lutz@norlabs.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood-inference.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood-inference.com>
Date: 2028-03-22T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: NorLabs private endpoint - allowlist / firewall requirements (final)

Sara / Nora — thanks for the quick responses. Confirming the decision and next steps so your change board has a single artifact to review.

Agreed implementation (NorLabs -> Redwood):
- NorLabs will provision a static NAT pool of 3 IPv4 addresses and provide the /32 entries to us by 2028-03-24 17:00 PT. Redwood will bind those to the control-plane FQDNs and provide the final egress_ip_mapping.csv.
- NorLabs will add outbound TCP/443 to the three /32s and to telemetry.redwood-inference.com (443).
- Mutual TLS: NorLabs will present client certs with leaf CN = norlabs-egress-prod; Redwood will validate CN + OID 1.2.840.113549.1.9.7 when present. Redwood will also provide a thumbprint list for pinning; thumbprint rotation is on a 14-day window with overlap.
- Audit & evidence: Redwood will deliver the CSV, mTLS matrix, and a short runbook. We will produce a 7-day sample access log bundle and a signed rotation manifest on request.

Action items: 
- NorLabs (Nora/Sara): share the three static IPs as /32 entries by 2028-03-24 17:00 PT.
- Redwood (Kimberly/Jonas/David): produce final mapping + runbook by 2028-03-24 23:59 PT.

Ive attached the working drafts we discussed (norlabs_mtls_matrix.xlsx, egress_ip_mapping.csv) and a link to the mutual action plan. If NorLabs' network team wants a short joint test window, we can schedule a 30-minute validation slot next week to verify TLS handshakes and thumbprint assertions.

Thanks — looking forward to signoff.

Kimberly
--

Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
